MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  MONDAY, APRIL 17, 2023 AT 8:00 A.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Domier called the special meeting to order at 8:01 a.m. in the
Barth Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Domier led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Alternate Wahl, Alternate Wu, Trustee Derry, Trustee
  Osegueda, Vice Chairperson Sadun, and Chairperson Domier

  ABSENT: Trustee Chien

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared recent news about libraries in Michigan and Missouri where public
officials have been pressured to take punitive actions, librarians have been removed from their
positions, and libraries have been defunded. He shared that he admires library professionals who
defend everyone’s rights to access information freely and without censorship, and how proud he is
to live in a community that values literacy and freedom of expression.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Vice Chairperson Sadun thanked Chairperson Domier for his Chairperson Report and added that
sharing of ideas needs to be fostered.

Alternate Wahl, Alternate Wu, Trustee Derry, and Trustee Osegueda did not have anything to
report.

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Vice Chairperson Sadun shared that vintage travel posters are currently on display, which may have
been collected over the years by the Foundation. The next exhibit will display Chinese calligraphers
from May 27 – July 7, with a reception on June 3 from 2 – 4 PM. In addition, a donation check was
received from the prior exhibit, artists of Studio 1034; one of the artists from this exhibit has
expressed interest in a solo exhibit.

4. FRIENDS OF THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Derry shared that the Friends have been planning the 65th anniversary dinner scheduled for
this Friday.

5. SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY FOUNDATION LIAISON REPORT
No report was given.

NEW BUSINESS

6. FY 2023-24 PROPOSED BUDGET

Director Johnson and Library Manager Vera presented the staff report.

Several Trustees shared that they appreciated the comments and narratives throughout the
documents to help the reader better understand the changes to the budget, as well as new priorities.

Vice Chairperson Sadun recalled how staff have experienced trouble hiring and retaining part-time
staff, which make up a large portion of the library’s staff; she shared that she believes this has to do
with the wages offered and asked what can be done. Director Johnson responded the City chose to
transition full-time positions to part-time several years ago, as well as transitioned part-time
positions from PERS to PARS which eliminates benefits. Library Manager Vera added that the City
is not the only organization that is understaffed; she explained that the City of Los Angeles is severely
understaffed as well, so the City is not unique. Finance Director Chung added that PERS is 20-25%
more expensive for the City, while PARS is a cheaper option that most cities utilize. He explained
that PERS positions are more attractive, but the Council needs to keep in mind the City has limited
resources. He added that Human Resources Director Guerrero will be doing a compensation study
next fiscal year to see how the City’s wages compare to the surrounding area. Vice Chairperson
Sadun shared that she hopes the Library will be able to attract and retain quality staff in the future.

Chairperson Domier inquired about the meaning of “not all donation money was spent this year.”
Library Manager Vera responded that it is tied to the personnel issue; some of the spending
responsibilities belong to part-time Librarians and Library Assistants positions, which have been
vacant. Chairperson Domier also inquired about the number of full-time staff at Monrovia Public
Library and why Dakim will not be renewed.
